a:r.a:t: Bacterial Chemotaxis Is Controlled by Enzyme-Coupled Receptors

p:cNvPr.descr: This diagram represents the two-component signaling mechanism in bacterial chemotaxis. The diagram has three sections, labeled a, b, and c. In image (a), there is a series of eight short and long arrows that form somewhat of a horizontal zigzag. The first arrow points up and to the left at a small star-like inscription, labeled "Tumble." From tumble, another arrow, marked "Run," points up and to the right toward a second tumble. From there, another arrow points down and right to another star-like strucutre, which leads to another arrow that points to another star structure. From there, another arrow points downward to another star structure, which leads to a longer arrow that points up and to the right to another star structure . From there, another arrow points up and to the left to another star strucutre; then, a final arrow points down and to the right to text that reads, "Attractant." In image (b), a blue tube with flagella-like extensions forming a tail is labeled "Counterclockwise rotation [right arrow] run." To the right of that, the same tube is shown, but the extensions are scattered all around it. This is labeled "Clockwise rotation - tumble." In image (c), an E. coli cytoplasm, represented by a yellow oval with blue outline, is shown, along with its plasma membrane. From left to right, there's a light red tulip-shaped structure, connected to a blue circle on the inside of the cytoplsm labeled "His." Above the tulip-shaped structure is a small red triangular structure labeled "Attractant." From here, an arrow is pointed to the right, where another tulip structure is shown. This time, the attractant is bound to the tulip structure, and the point at which binding occurs is labeled "Receptor-His kinase (component 1)." The receptor (tulip) is bound to His, which is bound to a P in a green circle. Next to it, a curved arrow shows movement of ATP into the reaction and movement of ADP out of it. Another arrow next to the second tulip receptor points to a third receptor that is bound to the attractant and to His on the inside of the cytoplasm. On the right end of the cytoplasm, there is a small yellow wheel that is connected to a light pink tail. The wheel is labeled "Rotary motor (controls flagellum)." Around the tail is an arrow that is curved into the page. Inside of the cytoplasm facing the rotary motor is a yellow oval structure labeled Asp. It has hair-like structures encircling it, which is bound to the P in a green circle. It is labeled as phosphorylated form of component 2 reverses direction of motor." There is another ASP near the left end of the cytoplasm, which is labeled "Response regulator (component 2)." A curved arrow points from this Asp to the other ASP.
